text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Seventy three Israeli soldiers killed in a mid-air crash of two helicopters on their way to south Lebanon.
-Pro-Iranian Hizbollah said its guerrillas fired rocket propelled grenades and mortars into 23 pro-Israeli militia outposts in south Lebanon.
-Brazilian Foreign Minister Lamperia said that the situation in south Lebanon could develop to the worse.
-Lebanon will file a complaint with a five-nation monitoring group over Israeli shelling of a civilian village in south Lebanon.
-Banque Beyrouth pour le Commerce is expected to increase its capital to $25 million from $18 million.
-Central Bank governor Salameh said treasury bill rates have reached an "acceptable level".
-Stormy weather in Lebanon; snow reaches foothills overlooking Beirut.
-President Hrawi said the Arab-Israeli peace process was at critical stage and that the only solution for peace with the Jewish state would be a complete Israeli withrawal from south Lebanon.
-Interior Minister Murr said the deterioration of the economic situation is the main reason for the increase in robbery incidents.
